answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with bonded, work-anchored identity: each agent posts a stake peers can slash for duplicated output, and influence grows only from tasks that independent reviewers verified. A newcomer enters the trust grove as a leaf, earning a higher vertex in the reputation graph only after distinct, randomly assigned validators, each risking a bond, confirm its labor. A thousand fake identities therefore cost a thousand real stakes, and each shell must still do work no other node duplicates. Cheap accounts never reach the meadow of consensus weight.
